items.title_en: Complex-trait dissection with Evolve-and-Resequence: Selection for improved flight performance in laboratory fruit fly populations
items.title_zh: 用Evolve-and-Resequence解析复杂性状：实验室果蝇群体中飞行性能的选择
items.abstract_en: Evolve-and-Resequence studies combine experimental evolution with molecular sequencing, enabling associations between complex trait phenotypes and evolved genomic changes. For this, a targeted complex trait is subjected to artificial laboratory selection in genetically variable populations. Using populations of fruit flies Drosophila melanogaster from the DSPR background, we have conducted a short-term selection study on a highly complex trait : flight performance. We selected for improved flight performance using a custom-built flight tunnel system, with light as a motivator and airflow as a resistive factor. As a result, flight performance significantly improved in selected populations compared to controls. We also observed signatures of evolution in flight related traits, such as activity level and wing shape, and in life-history related traits such as adult dry mass and fecundity. We used whole genome pooled sequencing on the selected and control populations, revealing significantly differentiated genomic sites. Gene ontology and enrichment analyses revealed the evolution of pathways involved in response to stimuli, growth, and development. We identified several genes of interest (e.g., Sdc, dally). The range of evolved phenotypes and associated genomic changes show that flight performance is an ideal complex trait for future Evolve-and-Resequence studies.
items.abstract_zh: Evolve-and-Resequence研究将实验进化与分子测序结合，关联复杂性状表型与进化基因组变化。我们以DSPR背景果蝇Drosophila melanogaster群体，对高度复杂的飞行性能进行短期人工选择：定制飞行隧道以光为动机、气流为阻力。选择群体飞行性能较对照组显著提高，并出现活动水平、翅膀形状及成虫干重、繁殖力等性状的进化特征。全基因组混合测序揭示显著分化位点；基因本体和富集分析显示刺激响应、生长和发育通路进化，识别出Sdc、dally等候选基因。结果表明飞行性能是未来Evolve-and-Resequence研究的理想复杂性状。
items.highlight_zh: 果蝇飞行性能经短期选择显著提升，并揭示相关通路与候选基因。
items.digest_zh:
研究了什么问题：像飞行能力这样的复杂性状，其遗传基础藏在哪些基因和通路里？传统方法很难把表型和基因组变化直接对应起来。

用了什么方法：作者采用Evolve-and-Resequence（E&R）策略，让果蝇群体在实验室里“进化”。他们从DSPR遗传背景的果蝇出发，用定制飞行隧道筛选飞行能力强的个体——隧道里用光吸引果蝇起飞，用气流增加飞行难度。经过选择后，比较选择组和对照组的飞行表现。

有什么结果：选择组的飞行性能显著优于对照组。除飞行本身外，活动水平、翅膀形状等飞行相关性状，以及成虫干重、繁殖力等生活史性状也发生了变化，说明选择产生了多方面的“副产物”。对选择组和对照组做全基因组混合测序，发现显著分化的DNA位点；基因本体和富集分析指向刺激响应、生长和发育相关通路，并锁定Sdc、dally等候选基因。

为何重要：这项工作证明飞行性能是一个适合E&R研究的复杂性状，能把行为、形态、生活史和基因组变化串起来，为解析复杂性状的遗传机制提供了可复制的实验框架。

items.title_en: Evolutionary dynamics of maximal syllable complexity show no universal bias rooted in jaw biomechanics
items.title_zh: 最大音节复杂度的进化动力学未显示植根于颌生物力学的普遍偏倚
items.abstract_en: Linguistic evolution has given rise to variation in the degree of syllable complexity that any given language permits. However, several models of language converge in predicting a universal bias towards the consonant-vowel (CV) structure (or a broader strong-weak asymmetry). This is closely tied to incremental speech processing, and in evolutionary terms has been linked to certain rhythmic orofacial displays in non-human primates. Yet, whether linguistic evolution really reflects such a universal tendency is an open question, one that we aim to address using phylogenetic comparative methods. Modeling change according to a continuous-time Markov process, we estimate transition rates for maximal onset and coda sizes (i.e. grammatical rules) across 5 language families. We demonstrate that a lineage-specific model outperforms a global model, and further explore the nature of lineage-specific long-term preferences and rates of change on multiple levels. We show that the former drive inter-family variation more than the latter. Generally, particulars turn out to impact syllable complexity more than any universal biomechanically or neurocognitively motivated biases do, implying that evolutionary continuity with our primate ancestors may have been overstated for this domain of language.
items.abstract_zh: 语言进化导致各语言允许的音节复杂度不同，但多种模型预测存在朝向辅音-元音（CV）结构的普遍偏倚，并与语音处理和灵长类口面部节律展示相联系。语言进化是否真反映这种普遍倾向仍存疑。我们用系统发育比较方法，按连续时间马尔可夫过程估计5个语系中最大音节首和尾尺寸（语法规则）的转换率。谱系特异性模型优于全局模型；谱系特异性长期偏好比变化率更能驱动语系间变异。总体而言，具体因素对音节复杂度的影响大于生物力学或神经认知的普遍偏倚，提示该领域与灵长类祖先的进化连续性可能被夸大。
items.highlight_zh: 音节复杂度由语系特异性历史主导，而非颌生物力学普遍偏倚。
items.digest_zh:
研究了什么问题：世界各语言的音节复杂度差异很大，但不少理论认为人类语言普遍偏好“辅音-元音”（CV）这类简单结构，并把这种偏好归因于语音处理机制或灵长类祖先的口面部节律展示。作者要检验：语言进化真的存在这种普遍偏倚吗？

用了什么方法：研究者采用系统发育比较方法，覆盖5个语系，把音节复杂度拆成“最大音节首尺寸”和“最大音节尾尺寸”两项语法规则。他们用连续时间马尔可夫过程建模这些规则随语言谱系的变化，估计不同谱系间的转换率，并比较“所有语系共用一套规则”的全局模型与“各语系有自己规则”的谱系特异性模型。

有什么结果：谱系特异性模型明显优于全局模型，说明不同语系有各自的演化路径。进一步分析发现，语系特异的长期偏好比变化速率更能解释语系间的差异。总体来看，具体的历史和谱系因素对音节复杂度的影响，超过了任何基于颌生物力学或神经认知的普遍偏倚。

为何重要：这项研究挑战了“语言普遍偏向简单CV结构”的强解释，提示在该领域，人类语言与灵长类祖先之间的进化连续性可能被高估。它强调语言演化更多由各语系自身历史塑造，而非单一普遍的生物力学约束。

items.title_en: Grazing protists foster zebrafish virus transmission
items.title_zh: 摄食性原生生物促进斑马鱼病毒传播
items.abstract_en: Virus transmission is facilitated by diverse means, ranging from particles hitchhiking on dust and other fomites to vector-borne replication. Aquatic ecosystems are rich with interactions between species at various trophic levels, but how these interactions influence virus transmission and infection biology is largely unknown. By mixing zebrafish picornavirus 1 (ZfPV-1) with a panel of freshwater microbial eukaryotes, we found that phagocytic cells promote virus infections in larval zebrafish, even though the virus is unable to replicate in these microbes. Ciliates, which act as crucial concentrators of micronutrients via continuous grazing behavior, stood out as promoters of robust and accelerated virus infections. We found that simply adding the model ciliate Tetrahymena thermophila to mixed populations of infected and uninfected zebrafish facilitated chains of experimental ZfPV-1 transmission between fish. This process depends on Tetrahymena phagocytosis and is likely due to the ability of the ciliates to deliver a concentrated bolus of viruses when consumed by larval fish. Notably, the pathogenic snakehead rhabdovirus was not transmitted after mixing with Tetrahymena, revealing selectivity, potentially through coevolution with ZfPV-1, that is not evident in all RNA fish viruses. We propose that non-host ciliates can act as virus vessels that increase virus transmission between hosts while potentially altering courses of infection by boosting zebrafish immunity. Virus vessels fill a crucial space on the continuum of virus transmission dynamics for viruses lacking the ability to replicate in intermediate species. Given the tools available to manipulate these genetically accessible systems, this paradigm opens new avenues for investigating otherwise hidden features of infection biology with experiments better approximating natural complexity in the wild.
items.abstract_zh: 病毒传播可由多种方式促进，但水生生态中物种互作如何影响病毒传播仍不清楚。我们将斑马鱼小RNA病毒1（ZfPV-1）与一组淡水微生物真核生物混合，发现吞噬细胞促进幼虫斑马鱼感染，尽管病毒不能在这些微生物中复制。纤毛虫尤其促进强劲且加速的感染。将模型纤毛虫Tetrahymena thermophila加入感染和未感染斑马鱼混合群体，可促进ZfPV-1在鱼间传播链；该过程依赖四膜虫吞噬作用，可能因其被幼虫鱼摄入时递送浓缩病毒团。致病性蛇头弹状病毒与四膜虫混合后未传播，显示选择性。我们提出非宿主纤毛虫可作为“病毒载体”，增加宿主间传播并可能通过增强免疫改变感染进程。
items.highlight_zh: 非宿主纤毛虫作为病毒载体，浓缩并传递病毒，促进斑马鱼间传播。
items.digest_zh:
研究了什么问题：病毒在水生生态系统中如何传播？除了直接接触或媒介生物，其他物种的日常活动会不会帮病毒“搭便车”？作者关注淡水微生物真核生物——尤其是摄食性纤毛虫——能否影响鱼类病毒的感染和传播。

用了什么方法：研究者把斑马鱼小RNA病毒1（ZfPV-1）分别与多种淡水微生物真核生物混合，再感染幼虫斑马鱼，观察感染情况。他们重点测试了模型纤毛虫Tetrahymena thermophila：把四膜虫加入感染和未感染斑马鱼混合群体，看能否形成鱼间传播链。同时用致病性蛇头弹状病毒做对照，检验这种促进作用是否有选择性。

有什么结果：吞噬性微生物促进病毒感染，尽管病毒不能在它们体内复制。纤毛虫因持续摄食而浓缩环境中的物质，能显著加速和增强感染。加入四膜虫后，ZfPV-1可在鱼之间形成实验传播链；该过程依赖四膜虫的吞噬作用，可能是因为纤毛虫被幼虫鱼吞食时递送了一团浓缩病毒。蛇头弹状病毒与四膜虫混合后未传播，说明这种“帮忙”有选择性。

为何重要：作者提出“病毒载体”概念：非宿主纤毛虫能浓缩并传递病毒，增加宿主间传播，还可能通过增强鱼类免疫改变感染进程。这填补了“病毒不能在中间物种复制时如何传播”的认知空白，也为研究隐藏的病毒传播机制提供了新范式。

items.title_en: Gene expression dynamics through time reveal low pleiotropy genes underlying local adaptation in silver birch (Betula pendula)
items.title_zh: 随时间变化的基因表达动态揭示银桦（Betula pendula）局部适应背后的低多效性基因
items.abstract_en: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying local adaptation in boreal trees is important for assessing their adaptive potential under climate change. The role of pleiotropy in polygenic local adaptation remains poorly understood. Here we studied growth and temporal transcriptomic responses to photoperiod in three photoperiod treatments in three populations of Betula pendula within a two-week time period to identify genes and co-expression networks underlying local adaptation and to estimate the level of pleiotropy in population specific gene expression. We used RNA sequencing to characterize the temporal transcriptomic responses which were analyzed with variance partitioning, differential gene expression and weighted co-expression network analyses. Photoperiod treatment and sampling time were the main drivers of gene expression variation both at the co-expression module and single gene level. The majority of circadian clock and flowering time genes exhibited striking similarity across populations. Nevertheless, we detected small but significant population effects in the temporal gene expression patterns which were concentrated on the periphery of the co-expression networks consistent with low pleiotropy effects. Our findings suggest that local adaptation to growing season length among populations exhibiting very low genetic differentiation along a latitudinal cline in B. pendula is likely polygenic and potentially governed through low pleiotropy genes.

items.title_en: A staged evidence chain identifies a recent horizontal transfer of a HET-domain gene into a Fusarium tricinctum strain from a lineage related to the Fusarium oxysporum species complex
items.title_zh: 分阶段证据链鉴定出HET结构域基因近期从与尖孢镰刀菌复合种相关的谱系水平转移至一株Fusarium tricinctum
items.abstract_en: Genes encoding the heterokaryon incompatibility (HET) domain form fast-evolving, highly paralogous families, which makes horizontal gene transfer (HGT) among them hard to separate from duplication, loss and annotation artefacts. We describe a staged evidence chain for testing a single HGT candidate and apply it to the strongest signal in the HET-domain view of a 109-genome similarity graph of 8,815 HET-domain (PF06985) proteins. Each stage is a separate test with a decision rule fixed before it was run: (i) a gene tree with ultrafast-bootstrap support; (ii) a species-tree check that donor and recipient lie in different clades; (iii) a genome-wide identity background and a contamination screen of the recipient assembly; (iv) a sister-species control that removes genes conserved by vertical descent; and (v) a tblastn search of whole genome assemblies, so that absence is tested in the DNA rather than in the gene annotation. We identify a recent horizontal transfer of a HET-domain gene into one F. tricinctum strain (MPI-SDFR-AT-0068) from a lineage related to the F. oxysporum species complex (FOSC). The F. tricinctum copy is 98.4% identical to its best FOSC hit (local protein identity), against a genome-wide median of 83%, and its synonymous divergence from the FOSC copies (median dS 0.11) is lower than that of 99.6% of F. tricinctum genes from their best F. oxysporum hits and of 91% of F. tricinctum genes from their best hits in the sister species, which argues strongly against vertical descent, hidden paralogy and shared ancestral alleles. Protein gene trees group it with the FOSC copies (UFBoot 96-98), and a nucleotide tree of the gene region places it as sister to all sampled FOSC copies (UFBoot 98). F. tricinctum and the F. oxysporum strains belong to different species complexes (species-tree patristic distance 0.075, about 22 times the distance between F. oxysporum strains). The gene is absent from the assembly of F. tricinctum's sister species, F. avenaceum (best locus 49% identity), and from 14 of 15 further F. avenaceum genomes, from 23 of the 26 assemblies of Fusarium species outside the FOSC and the F. tricinctum complex, and no other sequenced genome of the recipient strain's own lineage carries it; close copies (at least 90% identity) occur only in 7 of 9 FOSC strains and in one metagenome-assembled Fusarium genome from neither complex. In F. tricinctum the gene sits in an approximately 6-kb strain-specific island on a putative accessory scaffold with F. oxysporum-affine gene content, whereas in the FOSC it occupies one conserved, subtelomeric locus of a core chromosome. Assembly contamination was excluded, and single long reads span the gene and its flanks. The donor lineage remains unresolved, and formal reconciliation is still needed. The evidence chain is cheap and uses only public assemblies; each stage targets a specific alternative explanation, and synonymous divergence against the genome background proved the most decisive test.

items.title_en: Molecular Characterization of Gene-Product Relationships in the Wheat Gluten Complex for Reduced Immunogenicity Wheat Development
items.title_zh: 小麦面筋复合体中基因-产物关系的分子表征用于低免疫原性小麦开发
items.abstract_en: Immune-mediated reactions to wheat gliadins, including celiac disease and wheat allergies, affect ~1% of the U.S. population and are prevalent worldwide. Reducing the risk of inadvertent gluten exposure for individuals with celiac disease or wheat allergies requires the development of reduced immunogenicity wheat varieties which are suitable for human consumption. This study was designed with a view to improve our understanding of gene protein relationships at the complex wheat Gli1/Glu3 and Gli2 loci, and to develop genetic and molecular resources for breeding reduced-immunogenicity wheat lines. We conducted comprehensive genomic, biochemical, and immunological analyses of diverse wheat genetic resources, including aneuploid stocks, chromosome deficiency and interstitial deletion lines, Wasko omega null, the landrace San Pastore, Pegaso near isogenic lines lacking Gli1/Glu3/Gli2 loci, and progenies derived from a Wasko mega null X Pegaso(6A/6D) alpha null. Genomic characterization involved the targeted GlutEnSeq approach and PCR based DNA markers while biochemical and immunological analyses employed acid-urea PAGE, SDS PAGE, and ELISA. Integration of these complementary approaches resolved gliadin gene protein relationships at an unprecedented level. Notably, two F2; lines exhibited substantial reductions (both omega and alpha gliadins) due to the successful stacking of parental mutations. The resulting F2; progenies and associated DNA markers represent valuable resources for breeding wheat for reduced immunogenicity

items.title_en: A Compact Regulatory Logic Governs Fibroblast Cell State Plasticity in Fibrosis
items.title_zh: 一种紧凑的调控逻辑控制纤维化中成纤维细胞状态可塑性
items.abstract_en: Fibroblast activation drives organ failure across human diseases, yet its regulatory basis remains largely undefined. Here, we repressed 280 conserved disease-activated enhancers using CRISPR droplet sequencing (CROP-seq) in ~550,000 fibroblasts, constructing a regulome of 15 gene programs governing the profibrotic state. Systematic TF perturbation converged on MEOX1 as a central regulator, and fibroblast-specific Meox1 deletion in mice improved cardiac function, reduced fibrosis, and rewired profibrotic fibroblasts toward quiescence in heart failure. Effector gene perturbation in human cardiac fibroblasts revealed distinct regulators of contractility, migration, and inflammatory signaling, and these programs were conserved across profibrotic states in human lung, liver, and skin. Simultaneous repression of just six enhancers using a multiplexed dCas12a-KRAB system collapsed the profibrotic network, suppressed migration and contraction, and rewired fibroblast paracrine signaling to attenuate macrophage inflammation. These findings define the regulatory logic of fibroblast plasticity and establish a new framework for reprogramming profibrotic cell states in disease.

items.title_en: Mechanism-guided Discovery of Fluoroacetate Dehalogenase (FAcD) Variants for Enzymatic PFAS Defluorination
items.title_zh: 机制指导的氟乙酸脱卤酶（FAcD）变体发现用于酶促PFAS脱氟
items.abstract_en: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent anthropogenic "forever chemicals" whose strong C-F bonds (~460-533 kJ mol-1) resist defluorination, and the recast EU Drinking Water Directive sets parametric values of 0.10 ug L-1 for the sum of 20 specified PFAS and 0.50 ug L-1 for total PFAS. Here, we present DeFluorX, a mechanism-first pipeline that uses Boltz-2 to co-fold 2,150 bacterial fluoroacetate dehalogenase (FAcD) variants with 26 PFAS and fluoroacetate, generating uniformly high model confidence (rho = +0.08) but poorly tracked catalytic competence. Thus, the complexes were ranked and tiered by SN2-defluorination geometry based on the known mechanism of control of FAcDs RPA1163 with fluoroacetate: Odelta...C-alpha distance and Odelta-C-alpha-F angle; relay; carboxylate clamp; F-stabiliser; F-cradle; and penalties for scissile bond strength, backside occlusion, beta-fluorination and bond multiplicity. The tiering identified eight complexes (med angle 173.2 degrees, distance 2.91 A) with a high probability of degradation, including Alphaproteobacterial enzymes, with mono-, di- and trifluoroacetate attacking at 172-178 degrees versus 163 degrees for the control. We performed WaterMap, restrained 1 us Desmond MD, MM-GBSA and scans of the three WaterMap-aware best MD frames per complex using B3LYP/6-31G** QM/MM. All 12 frames exhibited product-end C-F cleavage with barriers ranging from 1.1 to 11.8 kcal mol-1, and the departing fluoride carried -0.43 to -0.63 e. The Laboratory validation is ongoing.

items.title_en: The Evolving Bileome: A Pan-Repository Landscape of Expanded Bile Acid and Related Steroidal Signatures
items.title_zh: 不断演变的胆汁组：扩展胆汁酸及相关类固醇特征的泛数据库全景
items.abstract_en: Bile acids and related steroidal metabolites are among the most studied biomolecules, yet recent work has revealed far greater structural diversity than previously recognized, much of it shaped by the microbiome. We previously introduced a repository-scale bile acid MS/MS library built from queries targeting C24 bile acid fragmentation, limited to Orbitrap Q Exactive datasets within GNPS/MassIVE. Here we announce a major expansion of this library: a bile acid and steroidal MS/MS spectral library assembled across three major metabolomics repositories, now capturing C23, C24 (including alkamine), C26 (C-C bonded aceto derivatives), and C27 bile acids, as well as C28 bile alcohols. The expanded libraries comprise 640,141 unique MS/MS spectra, of which 120,293 (18.8%) match 2,529 reference spectra, leaving most of this steroidal chemical space structurally unassigned. Linked to harmonized pan-repository metadata, the library provides a starting point for classifying MS/MS spectra as likely bile acids or related steroids, with two example analyses illustrated here. This resource allows researchers to flag candidate bile acid and steroidal signatures in their own data for further characterization.

items.title_en: MassBank Human: The annotated human metabolome
items.title_zh: MassBank Human：注释的人类代谢组
items.abstract_en: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics is essential for deciphering human metabolic functions and metabolite dark matter. However, the dark matter of the human metabolome is intricately hidden. Therefore, we developed MassBank Human, a curated library that distills 36,512,540 MS2 spectra from 76 public human datasets into 203,886 high-quality spectra via spectral averaging, recalibration, and filtering to achieve high mass accuracy. We further used three metabolite annotation tools and developed a Zipf-Bayesian rank aggregation framework to aggregate their rankings with false discovery rate control. This framework assigned molecular formulas, chemical classes, and planar structures to 55,564, 22,619, and 14,198 spectra, respectively. Approximately half of the annotated structures potentially originated from food, pollutants, or gut microbiota. In a metabolome analysis of colorectal cancer cells, MassBank Human doubled structural annotation coverage (10.6% to 21.2%), identifying acetylated polyamines as markers of metabolic rewiring. This community resource provides an annotated foundation for exploring human metabolomes.

items.title_en: ELiAH2: update of the atlas of E3 ligases in human tissues by integrating tissue-specificity and docking properties of ligands for targeted protein degradation
items.title_zh: ELiAH2：通过整合配体的组织特异性与对接特性用于靶向蛋白降解的人类组织E3连接酶图谱更新
items.abstract_en: Targeted protein degradation (TPD), including proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), requires coordinated selection of E3 ligases, target proteins, and ligands to achieve efficient and tissue-selective degradation. However, current TPD resources provide limited support for integrating tissue-specific transcriptomic evidence with structural compatibility during early candidate prioritization. Here, we present ELiAH2, an expanded database for transcriptome- and structure-guided prioritization of TPD candidates. ELiAH2 integrates GTEx RNA-seq profiles across 24 human tissues to characterize tissue-specific expression patterns of E3 ligases and target genes. Compared with the previous version, ELiAH, current update presented over 200% of expansion for the number of covered tissues and samples. Previously, E3 ligase-target gene associations were inferred using mutual information-based network analysis, enabling users to explore transcriptomic relationships. To further support structural evaluation, ELiAH2 provides large-scale docking datasets comprising 827,385 E3 ligase-target protein pairs and 7,800,521 protein-ligand docking models, including E3 ligase-ligand and target protein-ligand interactions. Docking scores, ranked interaction tables, gene and ligand identifiers, and downloadable PDB structures are incorporated into the web interface. By combining tissue specificity, E3-target association, protein-protein docking, and protein-ligand docking, ELiAH2 provides a comprehensive resource for narrowing the TPD search space and supporting rational degrader design. ELiAH2 is freely available at https://eliahdb.org.

items.title_en: BioMINTREL expands biological problem solving through cross-disciplinary representations
items.title_zh: BioMINTREL通过跨学科表征扩展生物问题求解
items.abstract_en: Biological research agents often rely on familiar analytical methods, limiting the questions explored in existing data. We introduce BioMINTREL, an AI agent that finds methods from other disciplines and connects them to biological measurements. It can draw on relationships among datasets and complementary ideas from several methods to develop new questions and analyses. We evaluate it on BioMDC-Bench, which assesses 228 possible applications of computational methods to biological tasks. Compared with GPT-5.4 mini and Qwen3.6-35B, BioMINTREL improves F1 agreement with human experts by up to 45.3 percentage points and increases coverage of applications supported by studies published in subsequent years by up to 58.8 percentage points. Four case studies on real data go beyond previous analyses to reveal dose-specific variant effects, constraints on spatial cell communication and routes through perturbation-response states, and identify the sampling needed to test whether rare high-state cells predict later lineage size. These results highlight BioMINTREL's potential to expand questions in existing data and suggest directions for subsequent research.

items.title_en: To mix or to de-mix?: Cation-π suppresses heterogeneity in local structure and dynamics of heterotypic Condensates
items.title_zh: 混合还是去混合？：阳离子-π抑制异型凝聚体局部结构与动力学中的异质性
items.abstract_en: Heterotypic biomolecular condensates can exhibit pronounced spatial and dynamic heterogeneity because chemically distinct components compete between self- and cross-association. Here, we use coarse-grained simulations to investigate how cation-{pi} interactions modulate this competition in condensates formed by peptides with systematic variation of hydrophobicity-to-charge ratios in binary peptide pairs. By independently tuning sequence heterogeneity, peptide composition, and cation-{pi} interaction strength, we establish how an additional short-range interaction reshapes condensate stability, internal organization, and molecular dynamics. In the absence of cation-{pi} interactions, highly heterogeneous peptide pairs form distinct core-shell architectures, with charge- and hydrophobicity-rich sequences preferentially occupying different regions of the condensate. Introducing cation-{pi} interactions progressively enhances phase stability and promotes molecular mixing, with stronger interactions substantially increasing the critical temperature and condensate density. Energetic analysis reveals that cation-{pi} interactions partially compensate for the loss of electrostatic and hydrophobic stabilization, providing an additional and tuneable source of cohesive interactions. This enhanced cross-association also suppresses spatial and dynamic heterogeneity, yielding more homogeneous peptide distributions, slower translational diffusion, and more uniform chain reconfiguration within the dense phase. Collectively, our results demonstrate that cation-{pi} interactions provide a molecular mechanism for coupling condensate stability to spatial organization and internal dynamics, enabling sequence heterogeneity and composition to be translated into distinct condensate states.

items.title_en: hnRNPA1 Remodels SARS-CoV-2 Genomic G-Quadruplexes through Its UP1 Domain
items.title_zh: hnRNPA1通过其UP1结构域重塑SARS-CoV-2基因组G-四链体
items.abstract_en: The single-stranded RNA genome of SARS-CoV-2 contains several predicted G-quadruplex (G4) forming sequences. Pharmacological stabilisation of these structures has been shown to suppress viral replication, suggesting that their resolution may be required for efficient viral replication. However, the roles of host proteins in stabilization or destabilization of G4 structures have remained largely unexplored. Human hnRNPA1, one of the most abundant RNA-binding proteins in eukaryotic cells, is a G-quadruplex unfolding protein and has independently been identified as a SARS-CoV-2 genome-binding protein. However, whether it acts on the G-quadruplexes within the SARS-CoV-2 genome has not been examined. Here, we screened eight putative G-quadruplex forming sequences conserved across SARS-related coronaviruses and identified two sequences that fold into G4 structures, confirmed by circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy and thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence-based experiments. Furthermore, we showed that the UP1 and UP1+RGG domains of hnRNPA1 specifically bind and unfold these two viral RNA G-quadruplexes. Both UP1 and UP1+RGG unfold viral RNA G-quadruplexes to similar extent, indicating that recognition and unfolding of these viral G-quadruplexes are mediated mainly by the UP1 domain of hnRNPA1. Together, these findings identify hnRNPA1 as a host factor capable of binding and remodelling SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA G-quadruplexes and suggest a mechanism by which the virus may exploit an abundant host protein to resolve G4 structures within its genome.

items.title_en: Modeled Oxidative Lesions Remodel the ABCB1 Linker: A Hypothesis for Transporter Regulation
items.title_zh: 模拟氧化损伤重塑ABCB1连接区：转运蛋白调控的一个假说
items.abstract_en: Multidrug resistance mediated by P-glycoprotein (P-gp; ABCB1) remains a major barrier to chemotherapy. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has increased drug responsiveness in resistant cancer models, but the molecular link between plasma-derived oxidative chemistry and ABCB1 regulation remains unresolved. We investigated whether site-specific oxidative lesions remodel the intrinsically disordered linker connecting nucleotide-binding domain 1 to transmembrane domain 2. Native-ensemble exposure analysis identified contrasting oxidation candidates: dynamically exposed Met653 and persistently exposed Trp698. Met653 oxidation to methionine sulfoxide and Trp698 oxidation to kynurenine were examined individually and together using a balanced 2 by 2 molecular-dynamics design with a mechanically tethered linker construct. Analyses integrated global descriptors, residue-resolved mobility, backbone order, native-state occupancies, projected breadth, and conformational switching. Trp698[->]KYN produced the dominant response: all seven global descriptors shifted toward restriction, accompanied by distributed mobility changes, compaction, and increased intramolecular hydrogen bonding. In the radius-of-gyration/end-to-end-distance projection, compact-state occupancy increased from 46.9% to 99.7%, switching decreased from 6.50 to 0.07 transitions per 10 ns, and projected breadth contracted. Met653[->]SME produced weaker, heterogeneous effects, while the double-modified linker remained restricted but showed greater projected exchange than Trp698[->]KYN alone. In this model, Trp698[->]KYN generated a compact, low-exchange projected ensemble in the tethered ABCB1 linker. These findings identify oxidation-site-specific linker remodeling as a candidate molecular intermediate that could influence linker-mediated domain coordination, while requiring experimental validation of lesion formation, transporter activity, and multidrug resistance outcomes.

items.title_en: Heart rate variability and electrocardiographic parameters among workers exposed to chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia in the Peruvian Andes: A cross-sectional study Cardiac autonomic function in Andean workers
items.title_zh: 秘鲁安第斯山脉暴露于慢性间歇性低压缺氧的工人心率变异性与心电图参数：一项横断面研究——安第斯工人的心脏自主神经功能
items.abstract_en: Chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia is an occupational exposure experienced by workers who alternate between high-altitude worksites and lower-altitude resting locations. Its effects on cardiac autonomic modulation and electrocardiographic parameters remain insufficiently characterized in Andean workers. This study aimed to compare heart rate variability and electrocardiographic parameters between workers exposed to chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia and controls working permanently at lower altitude in Arequipa, Peru. An observational cross-sectional study was conducted in 96 male workers aged 20-60 years. The exposed group included 53 workers performing rotational shifts at altitudes [≥]3,000 m above sea level with rest periods at <2,500 m, while the control group included 43 workers working permanently at <2,500 m. Heart rate variability was assessed during the morning rest period in Arequipa, at approximately 2,300 25 m above sea level, using a Polar(R) H10 heart rate sensor after 15 minutes of rest. Participants also underwent standard 12-lead electrocardiography. Vital signs were clinically similar between groups. No statistically significant differences were observed in PR interval, corrected QT interval, time-domain heart rate variability parameters, or frequency-domain heart rate variability parameters. In this sample of apparently healthy male workers evaluated during their rest period at moderate altitude, exposure to chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia was not associated with significant differences in resting heart rate variability or standard electrocardiographic parameters.

items.title_en: Factors associated with poor glycaemic control among children and adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus at a tertiary hospital in Kenya
items.title_zh: 肯尼亚一家三级医院1型糖尿病儿童和青少年血糖控制不良的相关因素
items.abstract_en: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) remains a growing global health priority, with disproportionate underdiagnosis, delayed diagnosis, and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite the introduction of the Life for a Child (LFaC) programme in Kenya, which provides free insulin, glucose-monitoring supplies, and specialist education, no published studies have examined the determinants of glycaemic control among Kenyan children and adolescents with T1DM. This study aimed to determine the proportion of children and adolescents achieving good glycaemic control and to identify the socio-demographic and clinical determinants of glycaemic control at a tertiary hospital in Kenya. This cross-sectional study enrolled 160 children and adolescents with T1DM attending the paediatric diabetes clinic at Kenyatta National Hospital, Nairobi, between September 2025 and May 2026. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected through structured interviews and physical examination. Poor glycaemic control was defined as HbA1c >7.5%. Associations between candidate determinants and glycaemic control were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Variables with p<0.2 on bivariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model; Firth's penalized-likelihood method was used given the small number of participants achieving good control. Only 9 participants (5.6%) achieved the target HbA1c of [≤]7.5% (mean HbA1c 11.02%, SD {+/-}2.29), and only 5 of 133 patients (3.8%) had [≥]70% of glucometer readings within the target blood glucose range (3.9-10.0 mmol/L).On bivariate analysis, household income (p=0.026) and self-monitored blood glucose (SMBG) frequency (p=0.018) were significantly associated with glycaemic control. In an exploratory multivariable regression analysis (Firth penalized logistic regression, given the small number of participants with good control), only SMBG frequency [≥]4 tests/day remained independently associated with lower odds of poor control (adjusted OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.04-0.84, p=0.028); the effect of household income was attenuated after adjustment. Glycaemic control remains markedly poor among children and adolescents with T1DM in this Kenyan tertiary hospital setting despite structured programmatic support. Frequency of self-monitoring, rather than household income alone, was the factor most strongly associated with glycaemic control, suggesting that strengthening access to glucose-testing supplies and supporting their consistent use should be prioritised in care, alongside attention to socioeconomic barriers. Longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these associations.

items.title_en: Vaccination and Non-School NPIs Shaped Ontario's Pre-Omicron COVID-19 Hospital Burden
items.title_zh: 疫苗接种与非学校NPIs塑造了安大略省Omicron前COVID-19住院负担
items.abstract_en: We develop an age- and immunity-structured COVID-19 model with setting-specific contacts, calibrated to Ontario incidence and hospital admissions before Omicron. We simulate counterfactual vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in schools, workplaces, and other community settings, evaluating projected severe-case demand against an illustrative healthcare-capacity benchmark. Vaccination combined with workplace and community contact restrictions keeps simulated demand within capacity. In contrast, relaxing restrictions in either setting produces large surges and repeated capacity threats, even when school restrictions remain. School-only changes produce smaller effects on severe disease. These findings highlight the value of vaccination and setting-specific contact restrictions that prioritize workplace and community settings for pathogens with adult-concentrated severe outcomes.

items.title_en: Epidemiologic shifts predict spatial patterns of measles re-emergence in the United States
items.abstract_en: Globally, measles is re-emerging in countries that have previously achieved elimination, including the United States. As immunization rates decline, characterizing the dynamics and evolving spatial pattern of measles re-emergence is critical to inform the public health response. We analyze annual county-level measles cases and vaccine coverage data in the United States (US) from 2011-2025 and find a shift in measles epidemiology in recent years indicative of re-emergence. While outbreak risk is spatially concentrated, we find that outbreaks are increasingly spreading throughout the broader population and across counties, but targeted interventions are predicted to prevent re-emergence nationwide. During the first decade of this period (2011-2020), outbreaks were only weakly associated with county-level vaccine coverage and predominantly isolated to single counties; however, recently (2021-2025), vaccine coverage has become strongly associated with outbreak size and spread across neighboring counties has increased. These findings suggest that measles transmission is increasingly sustained across the broader population rather than only in socially clustered communities. We developed a spatial statistical model to predict outbreak risk and size in all US counties with validation over 2021-2025; the model predicted counties with [≥]10 cases with a sensitivity of 95% (range across 2021-2025: 75-100%) and specificity of 83% (64-98%). Mechanistic models based on county vaccine coverage alone had worse performance, particularly in predicting larger outbreaks. Using the spatial statistical model, we find that prioritizing interventions in the areas of greatest model-predicted risk (e.g., top decile of US counties) was more impactful than state-level interventions (e.g., top five states) or targeting based on low vaccine coverage alone. Achieving even modest (5 percentage point) increases in vaccine coverage in counties in the top decile of model-predicted risk reduced long-term measles risk nationwide by over 90%. Together, these findings demonstrate that predictive risk modeling to inform spatially targeted interventions can likely mitigate the re-emergence of vaccine-preventable diseases.

items.title_en: Pickleball injuries, search interest, and participation in the United States, 2014-2023: an ecological time series study
items.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To describe (1) US emergency department-treated pickleball injury burden and the injury-to-participation measure among total players, with burden among adults aged 60 to 79 years as a descriptive subgroup, and (2) determine whether general internet search interest for 'pickleball' is also associated with total pickleball-related injuries. DESIGN: Ecological time series study, United States, 2014 to 2023. DATA SOURCES: National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) emergency department microdata yielded 1,738 adjudicated pickleball cases, 921 of them orthopedic, weighted to an estimated 101,450 injuries nationally. Google Trends, English Wikipedia pageviews, and GDELT news volume served as general pickleball attention signals, with the Trends index for 'sourdough' as a negative control. Sports and Fitness Industry Association (SFIA) participation estimates supplied a total player denominator. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Annual national injury estimates with design-based 95 percent confidence intervals; injury-to-participation measures; and correlations between total pickleball-related injuries and general pickleball attention signals before and after removing trend and seasonality. RESULTS: Estimated emergency department-treated pickleball injuries rose 17.5-fold, from 1,391 in 2014 (highly unstable) to 24,294 in 2023. 70 percent of adjudicated cases involved adults aged 60 to 79. During 2017-2023, injury estimates rose 4.0-fold and participation rose about 4.4-fold. No temporal trend was detected in the injury-to-participation measure (P=0.59). Search interest looked like an excellent proxy: in annual levels it correlated with total pickleball-related injuries at R=0.96, and Pickleball Wikipedia pageviews at R=0.98. However, so did searches for "sourdough", at R=0.76. Removing trend and seasonality left little (monthly residual R=0.084; year-on-year R=0.28 over 96 months, 2015-2023), and the seasons ran opposite, with injuries peaking in February and searches in July, such that, on 12-month mean profiles, the sourdough negative control fitted the injury season (R=0.96) while pickleball ran against it (R=-0.40). General pickleball search interest and pickleball news coverage remained correlated in year-on-year changes in 2017-2023 (R=0.64), whereas their corresponding correlations with total pickleball-related injuries in 2017-2023 were 0.25 and 0.20. CONCLUSIONS: The absolute burden of emergency department-treated pickleball injury has grown substantially, but the available surveillance data cannot resolve whether the sport has become more hazardous per participant. The observed rise is consistent with growth in exposure alone. The strong correlation between search interest and injury counts was not specific, the association was substantially attenuated after detrending, and the seasonal patterns were opposed. These descriptive results do not establish that search interest can substitute for injury surveillance, and series that rise together should not be assumed to be related.

items.title_en: Municipality-level ecological analysis of COVID-19 mortality and infections in Austria, 2020 to 2023
items.abstract_en: Background: Previous studies indicated that regional fluctuations in COVID-19 impact were associated with socioeconomic, demographic and environmental factors early in the pandemic. It is unclear whether factors associated with regional COVID-19 mortality and SARS-CoV-2 infections changed over the course of the pandemic. Methods: We evaluated the association of ecological factors with municipality-specific COVID-19 mortality in the national population of Austria between January 2020 and June 2023. Analyses were conducted separately per calendar year and pooled across years via random-effects meta-analysis. Outcomes were analysed using univariable and multivariable zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression, including annually averaged environmental exposome exposure (including air pollution and UV radiation), socioeconomic, demographic and infection dissemination predictors with significance threshold set to p<0.005. Secondary analysis modelled SARS-CoV-2 infections using of negative-binomial model (NB). Two additional approaches for smaller predictor set selection were applied as sensitivity analyses. Results: Within the entire observation period 18,430 COVID-19 deaths were reported. In univariable analyses (pooled RR (99.5% CI)), COVID-19 mortality was significantly associated with the proportion of commuters (0.79 (0.73-0.86)), residents aged 75-84 (1.18 (1.01-1.37)) and [≥]85 years (1.29 (1.04-1.60)), residents with at most compulsory education (1.15 (1.02-1.29)), employed residents aged 15-64 (0.89 (0.85-0.93)), and homeowners (0.91 (0.83-0.99)), as well as with precipitation (0.94 (0.89-0.99)) and the average time with a mean temperature of 5-15 C (0.95 (0.90-0.99)). In multivariable analyses the share of population aged 85 or older (1.30 (1.09-1.54)) and home ownership (0.92 (0.87-0.98)) were independently significant. Mortality predictor estimates were relatively stable across pandemic years. Across 5,963,882 documented SARS-CoV-2 infections share of employed in 15- to 64-year-olds (1.01 (1.01-1.02)), part-time employment rate (1.01 (1.00-1.02)) and district level nursing care allowance recipiency (0.97 (0.95-0.98)) were associated with detected infections. Overnight stays, population 85 or older, income, compulsory education or less and air pollution all had multiple significant estimates with opposite directionality, leading to non-significant overall associations. Sensitivity analyses outcomes mirrored main analyses outcomes. Conclusions: Throughout the pandemic in Austria, demographic and socioeconomic factors were associated with COVID-19 mortality and infections, but many associations, especially for infections, were unstable over time. These findings underscore the importance of structural vulnerabilities in epidemic impact.

items.title_en: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort
items.abstract_en: Background Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk. Methods Patients undergoing polypectomy within the Scottish Bowel Screening Programme, with surveillance colonoscopy between 6 months and 6 years were included (n=2642). Chromogenic immunohistochemistry (IHC; n=2466), 6-plex multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n=331), and spatially resolved 6000-plex single cell transcriptomics (n=7) were applied to adenoma microarrays. Cell density and location were measured using QuPath. Hierarchical then K-means clustering was used to define immune cell density-based clusters, which were compared to future lesion events using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log rank test. Results After adjustment for age, sex, site, size and dysplasia, adenoma CD3+ T cell density was significantly associated with future colorectal neoplasia (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.20-1.72, p<0.001). Using mIF three immune cell density clusters were identified; 1) high T cell density, low macrophage density, 2) low T cell density, low macrophage density, and 3) high T cell, macrophage and SMA density, with significant differences in future lesion risk (Cluster 1: 22%, Cluster 2: 41%, Cluster 3: 36%, p=0.032). Bulk RNAseq and spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed significant variation in T cell and macrophage co-location and gene expression profiles between clusters. Conclusion Adenoma immune contexture emerges as a possible determinant of future metachronous lesion risk, offering a novel biomarker to refine surveillance.

items.title_en: Accelerated high-capacity 6 mA transcranial direct current stimulation for major depression
items.abstract_en: Objective: Home-based 2 mA transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is FDA-approved for depression, but amplitude has been limited largely by skin tolerance. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and feasibility of accelerated high-capacity tDCS (HC-tDCS) at 6 mA. Methods: In this open-label pilot study, 20 patients with major depressive disorder received 20-minute bifrontal 6 mA sessions twice daily for five days using a high-capacity stimulator and hydrogel electrodes. A Safety Review Committee reviewed data from the first three participants before the remaining 17 were enrolled. Results: Retention and adherence were 100% (203 of 203 sessions); 17 of 20 received 6 mA throughout, with amplitude reduced for intolerance in one and limited by an electrode fault in two. There were no serious adverse events. The most common symptoms were fatigue (49% of sessions), burning (46%) and tingling (43%) at the electrode, and difficulty concentrating (40%). Electrode-site erythema occurred in all participants, with no severe reactions. At 1 week, 7 of 20 reported a residual skin change, none painful; at 1 month, spots of residual pigmentation were observed at the electrode site in 2 participants, both Black. In five days, mean PHQ-9 scores decreased from 15.8 to 7.2 (Hedges g=1.62); 50% of participants responded, 45% remitted, and improvement was maintained at 1 month. Anhedonia, mindfulness, and self-reported cognitive function also improved (g=0.76 to 1.23), with gains maintained at 1 month. Conclusions: Accelerated 6 mA HC-tDCS was feasible, well tolerated, and warrants a sham-controlled trial.

items.title_en: Effects of Cannabidiol on Auditory Mismatch Negativity in Autistic Children
items.abstract_en: Pharmacological treatments targeting core autistic features remain limited. In neurotypical adults, cannabidiol (CBD) alters mismatch negativity (MMN), an electrophysiological marker of automatic auditory deviance detection that has been associated with autistic traits. The effects of CBD on MMN, as measured using electroencephalography (EEG), in autistic children remain unknown. This secondary analysis of a pilot randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial examined the effects of 12 weeks of oral CBD oil on MMN during a duration-deviant auditory oddball task. We hypothesised that CBD would produce more negative MMN amplitudes and shorter peak latencies relative to placebo. Nineteen autistic children (6-12 years, 8 female) received CBD (dose) and placebo in randomised order, separated by an 8-week washout. Age-adjusted linear mixed-effects models tested Time (baseline, follow-up) x Treatment (CBD, placebo) effects on mean MMN amplitude and peak latency separately at Fz and FCz. Exploratory Spearman correlations examined baseline associations between MMN and Developmental Behaviour Checklist-2 (DBC-2) Social Relating scores. At FCz, latency decreased following CBD but increased following placebo but did not survive FDR correction (p = .029, pFDR = .058) and no other interactions were significant. Higher baseline DBC-2 Social Relating scores were associated with more negative MMN amplitude at FCz (rho = -.58, pFDR = .028) and Fz (rho = -.59, pFDR = .028). These findings provide tentative evidence that CBD may modulate MMN latency in autistic children. Larger trials should clarify CBDs effects on MMN and further examine the association between MMN amplitude and social-relating difficulties.

items.title_en: T-cell dysregulation is implicated in the encephalopathy of prematurity
items.abstract_en: Preterm birth is strongly linked to systemic inflammation and encephalopathy of prematurity, which underlies subsequent cognitive impairment. T-cell immunity contributes to brain-immune crosstalk across the life course but its role in the pathogenesis of encephalopathy of prematurity is unknown. Protein epigenetic scores are DNA methylation (DNAm)-based proxies of circulating proteins. We tested the hypothesis that T-cell dysregulation has a specific role in child neurodevelopment following preterm birth. Multimodal data were collected from 144 preterm infants (median gestational age at birth 29+5 weeks [range 23+3 to 32+6]) recruited to a prospective cohort study: saliva DNAm for protein epigenetic score derivation and brain MRI, both at term-equivalent age, and the Mullen Scales of Early Learning Composite score at 5 years from a subset. We investigated associations of the epigenetic scores for cytotoxic and regulatory T cell-associated molecule (DNAm CRTAM) and C-reactive protein (DNAm CRP; a non-specific marker of inflammation) with MRI metrics of encephalopathy of prematurity: global and regional brain volumes, and general factors of diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging metrics averaged across 42 white matter tracts. We tested whether DNAm CRTAM explains more variance than DNAm CRP in MRI metrics of the encephalopathy of prematurity and cognitive scores in childhood. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower general factor of fractional anisotropy ({beta} = -0.252, q = 0.011) and higher general factors of radial diffusivity ({beta} = 0.215, q = 0.039), mean diffusivity ({beta} = 0.198, q = 0.047) and orientation dispersion index ({beta} = 0.201, q = 0.048), independent of inflammatory morbidities and other biological covariates after false discovery rate correction. DNAm CRTAM explained more variance than DNAm CRP (maximum incremental R2 = 4.2% vs 1.5%) in diffusion MRI metrics. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower cognitive scores at 5 years, independent of DNAm CRP and other covariates ({beta} = -0.332, P = 0.008), and explained more variance in cognitive scores than DNAm CRP (incremental R2 = 9.4% vs 1.2%). An epigenetic proxy of CRTAM in preterm infants is associated with both encephalopathy of prematurity in the neonatal period and lower cognitive performance at 5 years, explaining greater incremental variance than a non-specific marker of inflammation. The data implicate T-cell dysregulation in the pathophysiology of atypical neurodevelopment following preterm birth.

items.title_en: Does the Disease-free Survival Benefit of Adding Belzutifan to Adjuvant Pembrolizumab Persist Beyond the Planned Treatment Period? A Reconstructed Individual Patient Data Analysis of Phase 3 Renal Cell Carcinoma Trials
items.abstract_en: Background and Objective: Adding belzutifan to adjuvant pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival (DFS) in LITESPARK-022, but its durability beyond the 1-year treatment is unknown. Methods: Following a registered plan, we reconstructed individual patient data from published Kaplan-Meier curves of ten phase 3 adjuvant renal cell carcinoma trials. Within each trial, we estimated restricted mean survival time differences ({Delta}RMST), hazard ratios (HRs) before and after planned treatment ended, and DFS differences. Key Findings and Limitations: In LITESPARK-022 (central review), the 24-month {Delta}RMST was 1.34 months (95% confidence interval 0.73-1.95), and the belzutifan arm remained ahead after month 12 ({Delta}RMST increment 0.74 months/yr, 0.32-1.19). The HR was 0.55 (0.43-0.71) before month 12 and 1.16 (0.87-1.54) afterwards (post/pre ratio 2.10); investigator assessment showed similar attenuation. Similar ratios occurred in KEYNOTE-564 at its first interim analysis (2.02), whose benefit persisted, and in SORCE and PROTECT (2.09, 2.59), whose benefit faded. From months 12 to 30 (post hoc), the DFS difference changed by -3.7 percentage points (-8.1 to 0.8) with central review and 0.6 (-4.0 to 5.0) with investigator assessment. Data were reconstructed, and follow-up was short. Conclusions and Clinical Implications: Relative hazard reductions with belzutifan were greater before month 12; durability of the absolute DFS advantage is uncertain and assessment-dependent, so single-HR projections should be avoided.

items.title_en: Multimodal profiling for prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: the prospective PIONeeR biomarkers study
items.title_zh: 多模态分析预测晚期非小细胞肺癌抗PD-(L)1治疗原发耐药：前瞻性PIONeeR生物标志物研究
items.abstract_en: Background Pretreatment prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains an unmet clinical need. Existing biomarkers - including PD-L1 expression and tumour mutational burden (TMB) - are insufficiently discriminatory, and multimodal predictive models targeting primary resistance are still lacking to precisely drive patients treatment strategy. Methods PIONeeR was a prospective, multicentre biomarker study conducted across 17 centres (NCT03493581). Adults with advanced NSCLC initiating standard-of-care first-line platinum-based chemotherapy plus anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, or second-or-later-line anti-PD-(L)1 monotherapy, were enrolled. Pretreatment multimodal profiling spanned six biological layers: clinical, routine medical biology, high-dimensional circulating immune phenotyping, soluble vascular markers, tumour immune contexture with digital pathology analysis of multiplex immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence, transcriptomics and genomics. The primary endpoint was prediction of primary resistance (PrR). Thirty-six feature-selection methods and ten machine learning models (360 pipelines) were benchmarked within a .632 optimism-correction framework. Results Between March 2018 and January 2023, 439 patients were enrolled (269 first-line, 170 subsequent-line); 435 were evaluable for PrR, which occurred in 39.5%. Individual biomarkers showed broad but modest associations with PrR (maximum AUROC 0.64). In the first-line chemo-immunotherapy setting, the multimodal signature achieved an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.69 (s.d. 0.06) and a Positive Predictive Value (PPV) of 0.51 (s.d. 0.11) against a primary-resistance prevalence of 30%, outperforming PD-L1 (PPV 0.36, s.d. 0.02) and TMB (PPV 0.35, s.d. 0.03). In the subsequent-line setting it achieved an AUROC of 0.69 (s.d. 0.08) and a PPV of 0.64 (s.d. 0.08), where PD-L1 alone performed at least as well (PPV 0.68). The 18-feature signature included stromal regulatory T-cell infiltration, circulating transitional B cells, and multiple routine laboratory variables, with treatment-setting-dependent contributions. Interpretation Despite comprehensive multimodal pretreatment profiling, primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced NSCLC cannot be captured by isolated biomarkers alone. Complete results are publicly accessible through an interactive dashboard (https://compo.inria.fr/pioneer-dashboard/), a reference resource for future meta-analyses. Multimodal integration improved risk stratification while highlighting the strong contribution of routinely available baseline variables. These findings support the development of clinically pragmatic models to identify patients who should access next-generation immunotherapy strategies aimed at overcoming primary resistance to PD-(L)1 inhibition.
items.abstract_zh: 晚期非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）抗PD-(L)1原发耐药预测仍缺乏有效手段，PD-L1和TMB区分能力不足。PIONeeR前瞻性多中心研究（NCT03493581）纳入一线化疗联合抗PD-(L)1或后线单药治疗的晚期NSCLC成人，治疗前采集六层多模态数据：临床、循环免疫表型、可溶性血管标志物、肿瘤免疫微环境（多重IHC/IF数字病理）、转录组和基因组等。主要终点为原发耐药（PrR）预测，在.632乐观校正框架下测试360条机器学习流程。435例可评估，PrR发生率39.5%。单标志物最大AUROC仅0.64；一线化疗-免疫治疗中，多模态特征乐观校正AUROC 0.69、PPV 0.51，优于PD-L1（PPV 0.36）和TMB（PPV 0.35）。
items.highlight_zh: 多模态特征预测NSCLC抗PD-(L)1原发耐药，优于PD-L1和TMB。
items.digest_zh:
研究了什么问题：免疫检查点抑制剂（抗PD-(L)1）是晚期非小细胞肺癌的重要治疗，但部分患者从一开始就无效，称为“原发耐药”。临床急需在治疗前预测谁会耐药，以便调整策略。现有标志物PD-L1和肿瘤突变负荷（TMB）区分能力有限，多模态预测模型仍缺乏。

用了什么方法：PIONeeR是一项前瞻性、多中心生物标志物研究，在17个中心纳入439例晚期NSCLC患者，覆盖一线化疗联合免疫治疗和后线免疫单药。治疗前采集六层数据：临床信息、常规医学生物学、高维循环免疫表型、可溶性血管标志物、肿瘤免疫微环境（多重免疫组化和免疫荧光数字病理）、转录组和基因组。研究在.632乐观校正框架下，系统比较36种特征选择方法与10种机器学习模型组成的360条分析流程，主要终点是预测原发耐药。

有什么结果：435例可评估，原发耐药发生率为39.5%。单个生物标志物与耐药的关联广泛但中等，最大AUROC仅0.64。在一线化疗-免疫治疗设置中，多模态特征取得乐观校正AUROC 0.69、阳性预测值（PPV）0.51；而原发耐药患病率为30%，多模态模型优于PD-L1（PPV 0.36）和TMB（PPV 0.35）。

为何重要：这是首个大规模前瞻性多模态预测原发耐药的研究，证明整合临床、免疫、血管、病理和组学数据比单一标志物更能识别耐药患者，有望帮助制定个体化治疗策略。不过模型性能仍属中等，距离临床常规应用还需进一步验证和优化。

items.title_en: Development, validation and clinical implementation of cellular swab materials for quality assurance of pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing
items.abstract_en: Background: Pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing (PGx POCT) enables genotype-informed prescribing at the bedside, but implementation is limited by the lack of suitable reference materials and standardised external quality assessment (EQA). Methods: Fixed lymphoblastoid cell lines were formulated as swab-based materials at defined cellular inputs for MTRNR1 POCT. Materials were evaluated using Genedrive MTRNR1 assays, quantitative PCR, acceptance quality limit batch release, workflow perturbation testing and stability studies, then deployed in an international EQA programme. Results: Materials were homogeneous, workflow-compatible and reproducible, with 100% correct genotype calls at the lowest intended manufacturing cell load. Seven EQA surveys yielded 253 participant results, with full-mark rates between 87.5 and 100%, and six test failures. Most failures occurred with low cell-input materials near the assay limit of detection. The materials supported genotype concordance, performance monitoring and identification of workflow and sample-related variability. Conclusions: Workflow-compatible cell-based reference materials combined with EQA provide a scalable framework for quality-assured PGx POCT beyond specialist laboratories. International MT-RNR1 PGx POCT EQA programme deployment demonstrated feasibility in decentralised settings. The framework may provide a model for the implementation, verification and ongoing quality assessment of PGx POCT. Further evaluation across platforms, analytes, settings and participant groups is required to establish broader applicability.

items.title_en: Restoring Physical Resilience: Consistent Functional and Sarcopenia Gains Across Two Vivifrail Cohorts
items.abstract_en: Objectives: To evaluate change in physical function and probable sarcopenia following a 36-week community multicomponent exercise programme (Vivifrail model) across two consecutive cycles, and to assess the consistency of this change between cohorts. Study design: Quasi-experimental, single-arm, repeated-measures service evaluation. Ninety-two older adults (2025-2026 cohort; mean age 75.9 years, 88.0% women) completed baseline and post-intervention assessments; an independent 2024-2025 cohort (n = 86) was analysed jointly for replication (n = 178). Main outcome measures: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score (primary); Timed Up and Go (TUG), handgrip strength, 6-metre walk time and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) (secondary); probable sarcopenia (EWGSOP2), SPPB-based frailty category, and a fall-risk indicator computed identically in both cohorts. Results: SPPB improved by a mean of 1.33 points (Cohen's d = 0.96; p < .001), with concordant improvement in all four secondary outcomes (all q < .005). 72.8% reached the substantial minimal clinically important difference. Probable sarcopenia fell from 17.4% to 5.4% (p = .006), and frailty category shifted toward higher functional levels (p < .001). Effect sizes were consistent between cohorts for SPPB, handgrip and 6-metre walk; the Time x Cohort interaction was significant for TUG only. In the pooled sample, elevated fall risk fell from 19.7% to 11.2% (p = .002). Conclusions: A 36-week multicomponent exercise programme was associated with clinically meaningful, reproducible improvement in physical function and a reduction in probable sarcopenia across two independent cohorts. The single-arm design precludes causal inference.

items.title_en: Protocol for the development of a tool (INSPECT-IPD) to identify problematic randomised controlled trials when individual participant data are available
items.abstract_en: Introduction Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) investigate the safety and efficacy of interventions. It has become clear however that some RCTs include fabricated data. The INSPECT-SR tool assesses the trustworthiness of RCTs in systematic reviews of healthcare-related interventions. However, where individual participant data (IPD) can be obtained, a more thorough assessment of trustworthiness is possible. Consequently, INSPECT-SR recommends obtaining IPD to resolve uncertainties, though there is no consensus on appropriate methods for forensic analysis of raw data. Our aim is to evaluate IPD checks to establish which are worthwhile, and how they can be implemented in a new tool, INSPECT-IPD (Investigating Problematic Clinical Trials with Individual Participant Data). Methods and analysis Using international expert consensus and empirical evidence, the INSPECT-IPD tool will be developed using five stages: (1) compiling a list of IPD trustworthiness checks, (2) evaluating the usefulness and ease of interpretation of the checks when applying them to a collection of presumed authentic and fabricated IPD datasets, (3) a Delphi survey to determine which checks are supported by expert consensus, (4) a series of consensus meetings for selection of checks to be included in the draft tool and finally (5) prospective testing of the draft tool in: a) the production of systematic reviews, and b) the journal editorial process for RCT submissions, leading to refinement based on user feedback. Ethics and dissemination The University of Manchester ethics decision tool determined that ethical approval was not required (18 June 2024). This project includes secondary research and surveys of healthcare researchers on topics relating to their work. All results will be published as preprints and open-access articles, and the final tool will be freely available.

items.title_en: Combining Randomized and Observational Data: The Case of Postnatal Prophylaxis Against HIV
items.abstract_en: The efficacy of current antiretroviral interventions for prevention of vertical HIV transmission is both a triumph and a challenge for future efficacy studies of novel agents, including long-acting antiretroviral agents. Given the effectiveness of current antiretroviral interventions, standard randomized controlled trials to assess novel interventions targeted towards further reducing vertical HIV transmission may be infeasible due to required sample sizes. To address this study design challenge, we propose a novel augmented clinical trial design, where a randomized trial with an active comparator is augmented with a concurrent observational cohort to supplement the standard-of-care arm. The proposed design and analysis can overcome sampling biases, and an associated diagnostic can evaluate potential biases from unmeasured covariates. The proposed trial design is illustrated with an example and studied further using a simulation study. In the illustrative example, an augmented trial with a 3:1 allocation ratio in the trial component yielded an unbiased treatment effect estimate, as compared to the trial component alone, and the standard error was reduced substantially. Although the total sample size of the augmented trial was larger than a similarly powered 1:1 standard trial, the sample size of the augmented trial's trial component was half the size of the standard trial and within the range of historically similar trials, thereby providing both feasibility and potential cost advantages. Although limitations with this design remain, many of these limitations can be mitigated by careful study planning and coordination. Augmented trials provide a potentially applicable solution to studying the efficacy of long-acting antiretrovirals for infant postnatal prophylaxis against HIV.

items.title_en: Impact of anemia on length of hospital stay among patients hospitalized for severe malaria in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo
items.abstract_en: Background: Severe malaria remains a major cause of hospitalization in malaria-endemic sub-Saharan Africa, and anemia is among its most frequent severity criteria. Data on the impact of anemia on hospital length of stay (LOS) among adults with severe malaria remain limited in Central Africa. We assessed the impact of anemia on LOS among adults hospitalized for severe malaria in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional, descriptive, and analytic study of medical records from adult patients ([≥]18 years) diagnosed with severe malaria (WHO criteria) and admitted to four hospitals in Brazzaville between January 2020 and December 2024. We dichotomized LOS as short (<5 days) or prolonged ([≥]5 days). Multivariable logistic regression, using a backward stepwise procedure, identified factors independently associated with prolonged LOS; isolated hemoglobinuria served as the reference severity category. Results: Among 523 patients hospitalized for severe malaria, 296 met the inclusion criteria. Median age was 25.5 years (IQR 20-40); 51.7% were female, and 82.1% had a low socioeconomic status. Median hemoglobin was 10.55 g/dL, and median LOS was 4 days (IQR 3-5). In multivariable analysis, prolonged LOS was independently associated with delay to consultation (aOR 1.25/day, 95% CI 1.09-1.44), isolated anemia (aOR 7.07, 1.23-40.55), convulsions (aOR 5.86, 1.81-18.97), prostration (aOR 4.42, 1.21-16.2), and impaired consciousness (aOR 4.29, 1.17-15.7). The strongest associations involved combined severity criteria: anemia with prostration (aOR 8.58), anemia with jaundice or hemoglobinuria (aOR 16.21), and impaired consciousness with anemia (aOR 33.31). Conclusions: Anemia is a major, potentially modifiable determinant of prolonged hospitalization in adults with severe malaria, with a markedly amplified effect when combined with neurologic impairment. Early anemia screening, improved access to safe blood transfusion, and reduced delays to care could shorten hospital stays and ease the burden on health systems in this setting.

items.title_en: A prospective case-control study of the gut bacteriome and mycobiome in glioblastoma
items.abstract_en: The gut-brain axis may modulate glioblastoma biology, but human data are scarce and the gut mycobiome remains uncharacterized. In a prospective case-control study, we sequenced bacterial (16S rRNA gene) and fungal (ITS) communities from rectal swabs of 23 patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma and 23 healthy controls. Fungal diversity was lower in patients than in controls (p < 0.001). Bacterial diversity and overall structure of both communities did not differ. Several short-chain fatty acid producers within the Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae were nominally reduced in patients, whereas the methanogenic archaeon Methanobrevibacter and Nakaseomyces glabratus were nominally enriched. In an exploratory multivariate Cox analysis, a higher intratumoral proportion of ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1-positive myeloid cells was associated with longer survival, independent of age, performance status and extent of resection (hazard ratio 0.82 per percentage point, p = 0.04). We hypothesize that the myeloid compartment links the changes in gut and tumor.

items.title_en: A clinical laboratory test-wide association scan of polygenic scores identifies biomarkers of psychiatric disorders
items.abstract_en: Background: Psychiatric disorders pose a significant public health burden, and their complex genetic architecture underlies multiple biological pathways, contributing to a lack of diagnostic biomarkers. Laboratory-Wide Association Studies (LabWAS) leverage electronic health record laboratory data as intermediary phenotypes to link genetic risk to physiology. Methods: Polygenic Scores (PGS) for 25 health-related, psychiatric, and substance use phenotypes were generated for individuals of African (AFR; N=10,473) and European (EUR, N=35,131) ancestry from the Penn Medicine Biobank. Laboratory data was prepared using the LabWAS pipeline, encompassing 78 laboratory tests and 6 vital signs. Linear regression models tested the association of each lab value with PGS adjusting for sex, age, and ten within-ancestry genetic principal components. Results: Four PGS were significantly associated with at least one laboratory value in AFR individuals and 22 PGS in EUR individuals. In EUR individuals, psychiatric PGS partitioned into three physiological profiles: anxiety, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, major depressive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder shared a metabolic/inflammatory signature (higher BMI, glucose, and monocytes; lower high density lipoprotein cholesterol and oxygen saturation); anorexia nervosa, obsessive compulsive disorder, and schizophrenia were characterized by lower BMI; and bipolar disorder demonstrated a more circumscribed profile with lower electrolytes and renal makers. Substance use disorder PGS similarly clustered: tobacco use disorder and externalizing showed metabolic/inflammatory profiles; alcohol-related phenotypes showed lower red blood cell indices; and cannabis use disorder had a more circumscribed profile. Conclusions: LabWAS reveals physiologic signatures associated with genetic risk for psychiatric disorders, offering new biological insights into their pathology.

items.title_en: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Cause-of-Death Assignment From Verbal Autopsy Records: A National Benchmark Study in South Africa
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND Timely cause-of-death (COD) information guides health policy, yet many deaths in low- and middle-income countries are not medically certified. In Africa, fewer than 10% of deaths are. Verbal autopsy (VA) yields a structured symptom questionnaire and a free-text narrative. Mortality surveillance increasingly records the narrative alongside the questionnaire, but the algorithms used to produce VA-based statistics were designed for structured responses only, so narratives inform physician COD assignment but do not contribute to algorithmic COD assignment. We evaluated whether supervised models could use both modalities to improve COD assignment. METHODS We analyzed 4,999 VA records for deaths at ages 12 years or older from a national sample of registered deaths in South Africa (RSA), using physician-assigned CODs as the reference standard. We trained unimodal and multimodal pipelines on the labelled records: pretrained language models (PLMs) fine-tuned on narratives alone, machine learning (ML) models on structured responses alone, and the two combined at the data, feature, and decision levels. We also prompted a locally deployed generative large language model (LLM) on the same unimodal and multimodal inputs, without parameter updates. All were compared with InSilicoVA, the operational comparator representing current automated practice. We evaluated individual-level assignment, population-level agreement, calibration, and generalization across provinces in RSA, reporting these metrics rather than ranking pipelines on any one of them. RESULTS Every supervised pipeline improved on InSilicoVA by 8.5-15.9 percentage points in top-1 accuracy and 3.5-7.1 points in cause-specific mortality fraction (CSMF) accuracy. The narrative and structured pipelines performed similarly in aggregate but differed by cause: 63.9% of deaths received identical predictions, 11.6% were correct only from the narrative pipeline, and 13.6% only from the questionnaire pipeline, with the narrative pipeline more accurate for noncommunicable causes and the questionnaire pipeline for communicable causes. Against the unimodal approaches, the decision-fusion pipelines added 4.2-5.4 percentage points in top-1 accuracy, concentrated in the most common causes, whereas feature fusion with cross-modal attention improved the less common causes, adding 6.6 points (95% CI, 1.7-11.5) in balanced accuracy and 5.5 points (95% CI, 0.6-10.3) in macro F1. Feature fusion reached the highest CSMF accuracy (95.7%). Paired differences from the better unimodal representative ranged from -0.2 to +3.4 points, with all intervals including zero. The LLM exceeded InSilicoVA on individual-level metrics and reached the highest balanced accuracy of any pipeline (60.6%), while the supervised pipelines retained higher CSMF accuracy. Supervised pipelines had lower expected calibration error than InSilicoVA. Supervised gains held across all nine held-out provinces, including every top-1 comparison and nearly every macro F1 and CSMF comparison. CONCLUSIONS PLMs using narratives alone substantially improved on current best practice and matched ML pipelines using structured responses, while multiple multimodal strategies produced further gains in individual COD assignment. The zero-shot LLM showed particular strength on rare causes, whereas supervised pipelines better recovered the population cause distribution. These findings support incorporating narratives as a core input to automated VA systems and evaluating representative fusion strategies for the intended output. External validation across settings and age groups will support broader implementation.
